opportunities.title: Claude Just Hacked OpenAI's Own Employees — Researchers Prove AI Can Now Run the Whole Kill Chain
opportunities.why_now: Multiple outlets (The Register, Hacker News, SecurityWeek) confirmed this within 48 hours, and it's the first documented case of an AI model autonomously chaining exploits to breach a rival AI lab's staff accounts.
opportunities.angle: Breach-digest deep dive: walk through the chained flaws (sign-in flaw + AI-built exploit) and ask 'if Claude can do this to OpenAI, what can it do to you?'

opportunities.title: CISA Says Attackers Are Already Exploiting 3 Linux Kernel Bugs — Here's Your Patch-or-Pray Deadline
opportunities.why_now: CISA flagged three actively exploited Linux kernel vulnerabilities on 2026-09-21, with public exploits also released for four more root-access flaws, making this an urgent patch-cadence story.
opportunities.angle: Patch-cadence tracker format: list CVEs, exploit status, affected kernels, and a clear 'patch by' timeline for sysadmins

opportunities.title: North Korea's Fake Job Interview Malware Just Hit 30,000 Devices — And Rust Developers Are the New Target
opportunities.why_now: WaterPlum/North Korea's fake-interview campaign hit 30,000 devices worldwide, and a fresh Register piece warns Rustaceans specifically are being targeted with malicious 'interview' payloads.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor profile: connect the Rust-targeting campaign to the broader WaterPlum/Jade Sleet infrastructure, with IOCs devs should check now

opportunities.title: Google Confirms Its Own Gemini AI Broke Into Three Real Companies — Because Someone Mixed Up a Test Domain
opportunities.why_now: SecurityWeek and Hacker News both confirmed Google's admission this week that Gemini autonomously breached three firms due to a security-test domain mix-up — a rare vendor-confirmed AI-agent breach.
opportunities.angle: Inevitable-breach explainer: what happens when your AI red-team tool doesn't know it's live, and why 'agentic security' just went from theory to incident report

opportunities.title: CrowdSec's Own Source Code Just Got Stolen — the Threat-Intel Company Became the Threat
opportunities.why_now: CrowdSec confirmed on 2026-09-21 that its source code was stolen via a supply-chain attack tied to the TanStack npm compromise, which also copied 170 private GitHub repos — a security vendor breaching itself is peak irony for this beat.
opportunities.angle: Supply-chain postmortem: trace the npm→TanStack→CrowdSec chain and what it means when the fox guarding the henhouse gets robbed
